An earlier completed story title is treated the same way at line 75. Full-reviewed fixes can exist before sign-off, for example with an allowance other than the prototype allowance (`src/forge/review.py:183`); neither path checks when the naming change landed.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a light-reviewed fix is merged through Forge. Every list test constructs fixes with `status: merged`, but Forge identifies a merged fix by its state file on the default branch (`src/forge/task.py:603`), and landed records can still say `waiting for checks` (for example, `.factory/fixes/hook-keeps-repo-nonbare.json:44`). An implementation that accepts only `merged` would pass these tests while omitting actual landed fixes and failing to count actual follow-up fixes. Exercise the real merge lifecycle or use a representative landed state.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - two app files carry the label. This test supplies only one app file; the other labelled file is documentation and is expected to be excluded. An implementation that lists only the first matching app file would pass every list test while omitting an open feature. The owning test needs to assert both app filenames.

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 1, Harm 1
The completed-story assertion calls `gaps()`, whose first action is an explicit fetch (`tests/test_prodgap_list.py:87`). The board is also first checked only after `forge next` and that fetch. A regression that reads stale story completion or board data before its own fetch would therefore pass the named proof, despite the planned fetch-order cases.
Adds work: exercise those cases before an explicit fetch; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 2.
